title: Lease Car Return Cleaning: How to Avoid Extra Charges
meta_description: Return a lease car clean so ordinary wear reads as wear, not neglect. What inspectors check, what cleaning can and can't fix, and when to book.
excerpt: Leasing companies inspect the car when it's collected, and dirt hides what they're looking for. Here's what a clean can fix before handback, what it can't, and when to book it.

keywords: lease car fair wear and tear

faq.q: Should I valet my lease car before returning it?
faq.a: If it's anything more than lightly dirty, yes. A clean car lets the inspector see that ordinary wear is just wear, and it avoids charges for things a clean would have fixed, like stains, hair and smells.

faq.q: Can a valet remove damage before a lease return?
faq.a: No. Cleaning removes dirt, most stains, pet hair, smells and, with a machine polish, most light swirls. Tears, burns, kerbed alloys, dents and deep scratches need a repair, not a clean.

faq.q: When should I book a clean before handing back a lease car?
faq.a: A few days to a week before collection. That gives seats and carpets time to dry after extraction and a smell treatment time to air out, and leaves room to get a repair quote if you spot damage.

faq.q: Will an air freshener cover a smell at lease return?
faq.a: Not really. An inspector can usually smell the freshener and the odour underneath it. The smell needs removing at the source, from the fabric, carpets and vents.

Handing back a lease car soon? Most leasing companies inspect the car at collection, and dirt hides what they're looking for. A grubby interior or brown wheels can get marked down for things a proper clean would have sorted.

Cleaning can deal with stains, smells, pet hair, brake dust and most light swirls. It can't fix tears, burns, kerbed alloys or dents, and nobody should tell you otherwise.

Our new guide covers what inspectors look at, what you can do yourself, and when to book so the car is at its best on collection day.
